ch1-open.title: Login
ch1-open.standfirst: Canvas M has one front door: sign in with your email and password. If someone sent you a meeting link, paste it first and it carries you straight into the room once you've signed in.

legend.text: Login — the card heading, with “Sign in to your account.” beneath it and the “Architectural collaboration platform” tagline above.
Email and Password fields — placeholders you@company.com and Enter your password.
Sign In — the submit button. It stays disabled until both fields have something, and reads Signing in… while it works.
Have a meeting link? — a small toggle below the form for pasting a room link before you sign in.
Need help? Contact your administrator. — the footer. There's no self-service sign-up or password reset.

ch1-password.heading: Sign in with email and password
steps: Type your work email in the Email field (placeholder you@company.com).
Type your password in the Password field (placeholder Enter your password). Everyone signs in this way — internal staff and invited clients alike.
Click Sign In. While it checks, the button reads Signing in…; on success the card disappears and your dashboard loads.
There's no “sign up” — your administrator creates the account and gives you the password. The footer reads “Need help? Contact your administrator.”
ch1-password.outcome: Your session is remembered on this device until you sign out, so you won't retype your password every visit.
ch1-password.note: Password is the only way in right now. A one-time login link by email exists in the product but is switched off until it works reliably on every network — so don't look for an email-link option on the card.

ch1-link.heading: Came in on a meeting link?
steps: If a host sent you a meeting link, click Have a meeting link? under the sign-in form.
Paste the link — or its bare ID,KEY — into the Meeting link field (placeholder Paste meeting link or ID,KEY) and click Continue.
Canvas M saves it and shows “Meeting link saved — sign in to join.”, then returns you to the password form.
Sign in with your email and password as usual; you drop straight into that meeting once you're in.
ch1-link.outcome: The meeting link only carries you to the room — it doesn't replace signing in. Everyone still authenticates with a password first.
ch1-link.note: If the link is malformed you'll see “That meeting link looks invalid.” — re-copy the whole link (or the ID,KEY) from your invitation.

ch1-errors.heading: Sign-in messages and what they mean
rows: The email and password didn't match an account.
Re-check both — mind capitals. If it persists, contact your administrator.
What you typed isn't a valid email shape (no @ or no domain).
Correct the address — it should look like you@company.com.
Can't reach the sign-in server. Check your internet connection (or try mobile data).
Your network can't reach the sign-in server — often Wi-Fi blocking it.
Switch network — mobile data is the quick test. This is not a wrong-password problem.
Too many attempts. Please wait a minute and try again.
Too many sign-in tries in a short window.
Wait about a minute, then try again.
The pasted meeting link couldn't be read.
Re-copy the full link, or the ID,KEY, from your invite.
ch1-errors.note: There's no “attempts remaining” counter and no self-service reset — your administrator manages passwords.
